newsitem.title: USA: Merck extends Costa Rican research pact.
newsitem.headline: Merck extends Costa Rican research pact.

text.p: Merck & Co Inc said on Wednesday that it and Costa Rica's National Biodiversity Institute (INBio) have agreed to continue their research collaboration to explore a portion of Costa Rica's biological resources in search of new medicines.

The current collaboration, based on the first agreement established in 1991, provides Merck with a limited number of plant, fungal and environmental samples from Costa Rica's protected areas for scientific evaluation.

The samples are collected and processed into extracts by INBio scientists and field professionals in Costa Rica, then screened by Merck scientists in the United States and Spain for potential use as human and animal medicines.

The renewed collaboration agreement is valid through 1998 and provides for incremental research funding of about $1 million to INBio, as well as royalties on the sale of any products that Merck ultimately develops from INBio samples and data.
